scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes two testing orientations (horizontal and vertical) to evaluate and classify the ignitability, flame propagation speed, and self-extinguishing characteristics of solid polymer and resin-based electrical insulating materials when exposed to a standardized open flame igniting source.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product testing & material classification specification (Electrotechnical Department / Solid Electrical Insulating Materials)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Mandatory Testing Compliance. Under municipal utilities, public works specifications, and smart meter box mandates, raw polymers and terminal moldings must be certified to comply with IS 11731 (Part 2) Class FV0.

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, burning times, or specimen dimensions must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Specimens must be rectangular bars measuring 125 ± 5 mm in length, 13.0 ± 0.3 mm in width, and 3.0 ± 0.2 mm in thickness.
Two lines are scribed across the specimen at 25 mm and 100 mm from the free end to calculate exact linear burning rates.
The standardized 20 mm blue Bunsen flame is applied horizontally to the free end of the specimen for exactly 30 seconds or until the flame front reaches the first mark.
FH1 indicates a burn rate of <= 40 mm/min for specimens >= 3 mm thick. FH2 indicates a burn rate of <= 75 mm/min for thin specimens (< 3 mm) or self-extinguishing behavior.
Specimens are identical rectangular bars clamped vertically. A cotton indicator pad is placed horizontally exactly 300 mm below the specimen lower end.
A 20 mm flame is applied directly underneath the vertically clamped bar for 10 seconds. Afterflame is recorded. The flame is applied for another 10 seconds immediately after self-extinguishing.
Afterflame time per burn <= 10 seconds; total afterflame time of 5 specimens (10 burns) <= 50 seconds; zero flaming drips (no cotton pad ignition).
Afterflame time per burn <= 30 seconds; total afterflame time of 5 specimens <= 250 seconds; zero flaming drips; glowing ceases within 60 seconds.
Afterflame time per burn <= 30 seconds; total afterflame time of 5 specimens <= 250 seconds; flaming drips are permitted to ignite the cotton indicator pad.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11731 (Part 1 & Part 2) : 1986 (Reaffirmed 2021) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing flammability tests for solid electrical insulating polymers. Equivalent to international codes IEC 60707 and UL 94, the standard unifies fire-retardant material criteria. Part 1 (Horizontal Method) measures horizontal burn rates (Class FH1/FH2), while Part 2 (Vertical Method) measures self-extinguishing limits of vertical bars under open flame ignition. Part 2 establishes three critical safety classes: FV0 (flame ceases in <= 10s, zero flaming drips), FV1 (flame ceases in <= 30s, zero flaming drips), and FV2 (flame ceases in <= 30s but allows flaming drips that ignite a cotton pad). These classes are mandatory for electronic panels, smart meter boxes, and household appliances.
